- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes, then sharply drop — suggesting overshoot and failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly when true values are rising or stabilizing.
- Forecast bias is stronger when historical prices are trending upward — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too late.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates downward momentum.
- When true prices show strong upward momentum (e.g., >90), model tends to overreact with high initial forecasts, then undercorrect.
- Model fails to capture “rebound” or “reversion” after sharp declines — often forecasts too low for a prolonged period.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to reflect volatility clustering or sudden reversals in price direction.
- Model overweights recent data, leading to overfitting to short-term trends, especially when prices are volatile or near support/resistance levels.
